Load catalogue components with `COMPONENTATOR()`; custom app-owned components remain normal app assets.

## 1. Look for the component first

The catalogue of jComponent components, with a live preview, the documentation and the download of each, is Componentator: <https://componentator.com>.

Before writing UI:

1. Find the component that does the job (input, form, listing, datagrid, notify, menu, approve...).
2. Read its page: what it does, its **configuration** and its context (what path and data it expects, what it needs around it).
3. Use it from markup with `<ui-component name="..." path="..." config="...">`.

Machine-readable forms of the same catalogue (use these from code or an agent):

| What | URL |
|---|---|
| The index for models: rules, the reference component and the API of the library | `https://componentator.com/llms.txt` |
| One component as markdown | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs/components/master/components/<name>/readme.md` (e.g. `input`, lowercase) |
| The source of one component, with its live example | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs/components/master/components/<name>/component.html` |

The readme of each component says the versions of jComponent it works with (`jcomponent: v19,v20`).

## Match the UI version first

Apps load `spa.min@19` or `@20`. A catalogue entry for jComponent 20 does not prove its markup or options work in 19. Check the actual layout, bundle and nearby screen before using a component or copying `PLUGIN`/binding syntax. A backend Total.js 5 dependency does not select the browser UI major version.

## Preferred components

When several components could do the job, use these:

| For | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Form fields (text, email, phone, password, multiline, checkbox, select, date...) | `input` (j-Input) | One component for every field: `type` chooses the kind. It replaces j-Textbox and j-Dropdown. |
| A box with a fixed height and scroll | `viewbox` | `height` is a percentage, `parent` is the container (or `window`), `scroll` / `scrollbar` control scrolling. |
| Loaders | `loading` | Reacts to the `@showloading` and `@hideloading` flags; `style` picks the look (1 = spinner, 2 = line at the top). |
| Tables and data grids | `datagrid` | For single page and enterprise apps: filters, sorting, pages, `height` modes (`auto`, `fluid`, `parent`). |
| Buttons and calls to functions | `exec` | See below. |
| Predefined design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode) | `intranetcss` | Ready-made CSS classes; see below. |

### exec: buttons and function calls

`exec` is a singleton that works for the whole page: any element with the class `exec` calls a function when it is clicked. Do not add `onclick` handlers or `addEventListener` for buttons.

```html
<button class="exec" data-exec="?/create"><i class="ti ti-plus-circle"></i>@(Create)</button>
<span class="exec" data-exec="?/options" data-prevent="true">...</span>
<a class="exec" data-href="/offers/">@(Offers)</a>
```

- `data-exec="NAME"`: the function to call, with the form `function(element, event)`. A `?` calls a method of the current plugin (`?/create` is `exports.create`).
- `data-prevent="true"`: stops the click from going further (for a button inside a clickable row).
- `data-href="URL"`: redirects instead of calling a function.
- Double click and context menu use the same attributes with a suffix: `data-exec2` (class `exec2`) and `data-exec3` (class `exec3`).

### intranetcss: predefined design

`intranetcss` is a component made only of CSS. It brings the shared look of the intranet apps, with a dark mode, so a screen does not need its own style for the common pieces:

- containers: `.panel` (with `label` and `.toolbar`), `.padding`, `.divider`, `.bg-smoke`
- lists and menus: `.listing`, `.listing2`, `.nav`, `.tabmenu`, `.tabmenu2`, `.iconmenu`, `.keyvalue`
- messages and badges: `.message`, `.message-success`, `.message-error`, `.message-alert`, `.badge` (with colors and sizes)
- sizes: `.small`, `.medium`, `.large`

Use these classes before writing new CSS (see [css](css.md)). Its source (version 5) is served by the component download service.

## 2. If it does not exist, create a component

A piece of UI that has behaviour is a component, not a block of script inside a page.

```js
COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) {
	// keep the names: "self", "config" and "cls"
});
```

- Names of components, plugins, variables and settings in **lowercase**.
- Keep at most 2-3 levels of nesting in objects.
- Avoid `_` in variable names.
- **Think reusable**: a component takes its data from `path` and its options from `config`, and knows nothing about the screen that uses it.
- Use the same name across projects for the same thing. Check the catalogue before choosing one.

## 3. Load components with COMPONENTATOR()

For shared catalogue components, use the app's `COMPONENTATOR()` bundle. App-owned components load through the app's existing assets. For example, in `definitions/init.js`:

```js
ON('ready', function() {
	COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,page,viewbox,input,form,validate,loading,datagrid,intranetcss,message,menu,approve,notify,errorhandler', true);
});
```

`COMPONENTATOR(name, components, removeprev, attrs)`:

- `name`: the name of the bundle (`'ui'`).
- `components`: the components of the bundle, comma-separated, without the `j-` prefix.
- `removeprev` (default `true`): deletes the older bundles of the same name when the list changes.
- `attrs`: optional extra parameters for the bundle.

The framework downloads the bundle once, saves it in `public/` as `ui-<name>-<hash>.min.js` and stores its address in `REPO.<name>`. The layout loads it:

```html
<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
```

Rules:

- One `COMPONENTATOR()` call per bundle (`ui` for the app, `webui` for public pages).
- List **only** the components the app uses: the bundle is what every user downloads.
- When you start using a component, add it to the list; when no screen uses it any more, remove it.
- A component you created yourself is a normal file of the app (`public/` or the plugin's `public/`), not a `COMPONENTATOR()` entry.

## Adapt the official component's appearance

Reuse the official component and its configuration first. A different visual design usually needs a scoped CSS skin, not a copied component implementation or a file that embeds jComponent itself.

The official `backtotop` is loaded through `COMPONENTATOR('webui', 'backtotop', true)` and declared as:

```html
<ui-component name="backtotop" class="app-backtotop" config="icon:ti ti-arrow-up;$init:FUNC.backtotop" data-label="@(Back to top)"></ui-component>
```

A stylesheet changes the appearance; a `FUNC` function adds button semantics, a translated accessible name and keyboard focus handling through the native `$init` hook. The official component retains its scrolling and visibility behavior. The hook is needed because the official component renders a span; CSS cannot provide button semantics.

Verify hook timing against the installed runtime and component: jComponent's `library.js` calls `make` before applying `$init`, so the hook can adapt the generated markup. Keep such hooks small and idempotent, and check Enter, Space, pointer interaction, focus and reduced motion. If a component supplies the required semantics already, use them directly.

## 4. Quick check

- Is there a component for this in the catalogue? Use it.
- Did you read its configuration and context before using it? Do.
- Is it in the `COMPONENTATOR()` list? Add it.
- Is there none? Create a reusable `COMPONENT('name', ...)` and use it from markup.

See [plugins-ui](plugins-ui.md) for how screens and forms use components, and [views-and-layout](views-and-layout.md) for the layout that loads the bundle.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/plugins-ui.md

# Plugins with UI

A feature of an app is a **plugin**: a folder with a server part and a UI part that the framework loads and the app shell mounts.

```
plugins/redirects/
	index.js              server: metadata + routes
	schemas/redirects.js  actions (see backend/actions.md)
	public/index.html     the screen: markup + <script>PLUGIN(...)</script>
	public/form.html      the form that opens over the screen
```

## Server part: index.js

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-exchange';
exports.name = '@(Redirects)';
exports.position = 3;
exports.permissions = [{ id: 'redirects', name: 'Redirects' }];
exports.visible = function(user) {
	return user.sa || user.permissions.indexOf('redirects') !== -1 || user.permissions.indexOf('admin') !== -1;
};

exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -redirects_list               --> Redirects|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +redirects_save               --> Redirects|save');
};
```

- `icon` is a Total Icons class (`ti ti-name`), `name` is translatable with `@(...)`, `position` orders the menu.
- `permissions` declares what the plugin adds; `visible` decides who sees it.
- Routes use the same syntax as everywhere (see [routes-and-auth](../backend/routes-and-auth.md)).

## UI part: a screen

A screen is HTML with a `<ui-plugin>` root and one `PLUGIN(function(exports) { ... })` block. Keep markup, scoped style and logic in the same file. Screens may also include a `virtualwire` toolbar, importer declarations and other app-shell wrappers; copy the nearest screen rather than enforcing exactly one root element.

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
</style>

<ui-plugin class="CLASS bg-white">
	<ui-component name="empty" path="?.items" config="parent:auto" class="invisible">
		...
	</ui-component>
</ui-plugin>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		exports.reload = function() {
			exports.refresh();
		};

		exports.refresh = function() {
			exports.tapi('redirects_list', function(response) {
				exports.set('items', response);
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

Rules:

- `CLASS` in selectors and class lists is replaced with a unique class for the plugin: it scopes the CSS so plugins do not collide.
- `?` in a path (`?.items`, `?/create`) means "this plugin": `?.items` is the data, `?/create` is `exports.create`.
- `exports.reload` runs every time the screen opens.
- Call the server with `exports.tapi('endpoint_name', data, callback)`. Add `ERROR` after the name (`'redirects_read ERROR'`) to show an error message to the user automatically.
- Set data with `exports.set('items', value)`, or globally with `SET('path @reset', value)`; read the model with `exports.model`.
- Handlers are attached in markup: `class="exec" data-exec="?/edit" data-id="{{ m.id }}"`. Read the attribute with `ATTRD(el)`.
- Text for people is always `@(Text)` so it can be translated.
- Naming: plugin, component and global names in **lowercase**; keep the names `exports`, `self`, `config`, `cls` as they are.

Official guide on names:

```js
// BAD
PLUGIN('Name', function(plugin) { plugin.doSomething = function() {}; });

// GOOD
PLUGIN('name', function(exports) { exports.dosomething = function() {}; });
```

See [binding and forms](binding-and-forms.md) for the importer, model path, submit callback and caller refresh as one connected flow.

## A form

A form is a second file loaded with an `importer` and shown by `miniform` / `form`. It has `?.field` inputs, a `validate` that enables the submit button, and a `submit` function.

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;icon:ti ti-exchange;autofocus:true;reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<div class="m">
			<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1;placeholder:@(Relative URL address)">@(URL)</ui-component>
		</div>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled><i class="ti ti-check-circle"></i>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>
```

Open it from the screen:

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};
```

## Confirm and menu

```js
SETTER('approve/show', '@(Are you sure you want to remove it?)', ':ti ti-trash: @(Remove)', function() {
	exports.tapi('redirects_remove/ ERROR', { id: id }, function() { exports.refresh(); });
});
SETTER('menu/show', opt);
```

## Think reusable

Components, plugins and global names are shared across projects. Before inventing one, look in the [catalogue of components](components.md) and in another app for the same name.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/views-and-layout.md

# Views and layout

## Layout

The shell of an app is one HTML file in `views/` (`admin.html`, `index.html`). It sets the title, loads the UI library, registers global components once and mounts the plugins.

```html
@{layout('')}
@{title(config.name)}

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
	<meta charset="utf-8" />
	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
	<link href="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css" rel="stylesheet" />
	<script src="https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js"></script>
	<script src="@{REPO.ui}"></script>
	@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.js + func.js', 'default.css', 'favicon.ico')}
</head>
<body class="invisible">

	<ui-component name="exec"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="errorhandler"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="locale" config="requests:1;language:@{language}"></ui-component>
	<ui-component name="LAZY menu" config="style:2"></ui-component>

</body>
</html>
```

- Directives start with `@{...}`: `@{title()}`, `@{import()}`, `@{if}` / `@{fi}`, `@{REPO.ui}`, `https://cdn.componentator.com` (a config value).
- Global components are declared once in the layout. `LAZY` loads a component only when it is first used.
- The component bundle is loaded with `COMPONENTATOR('ui', 'exec,locale,input,...', true)` in `definitions/init.js`. List only the components the app uses; see [components](components.md).
- `<body class="invisible">` hides the page until the UI is ready.

## Runtime, bundles and application assets

New layouts load jComponent 20 from the CDN. An existing app on another major version requires a deliberate migration.

- Load `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.css` and `https://cdn.componentator.com/spa.min@20.js` once per document. The runtime must precede component bundles and scripts that use its APIs.
- `COMPONENTATOR()` downloads the selected components; it does not replace the core runtime. Load the matching `@{REPO.ui}` or `@{REPO.webui}` after the runtime.
- Keep application helpers in app assets, such as `public/js/func.js`, and preserve the existing browser `FUNC` object when extending it. Load helpers before components that call them during initialization.
- Keep the app stylesheet and scoped component skins after the base stylesheet; see [CSS](css.md). Remove embedded copies of the runtime and obsolete custom loaders when adopting this setup.
- An isolated recipe iframe can intentionally use a pinned runtime with its own hashes and evidence. It is a separate document; preserve that version boundary.

Changing asset loading must preserve the existing title, language, canonical and alternate URLs, metadata, structured data, agent discovery links, landmarks and accessible navigation. Check the rendered HTML and browser console, keyboard interaction, mobile layout and reduced-motion behavior. A component initializing successfully does not establish that the whole layout is accessible.

## Translations

Every text a person reads is wrapped in `@(...)`, in views, in plugin HTML and in server messages: `@(Save)`. The text in English is the key.

## Two kinds of pages

- **App screens** (admin, tools): plugin HTML mounted in the layout, driven by `PLUGIN`.
- **Public pages**: server-rendered views returned by a controller (`$.view('index')`). They carry no `PLUGIN` logic.

## Naming

Lowercase file names with `-`: `search-results.html`, `form-offer.html`.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/binding-and-forms.md

# Binding and forms as one flow

The following connected example includes only the fields needed to show the lifecycle. It assumes the app shell, jComponent version, importer and `*form` alias setup; it is not a standalone page.

## Screen → model → importer

The screen declares the form importer and opens a model with the same name. The app's importer replaces `CLASS` when loading the form.

```html
<ui-component name="importer" path="common.form" config="if:formredirect;url:/~ID~/form.html"></ui-component>
```

```js
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formredirect @default', {});
	SET('*form', 'formredirect');
};

exports.edit = function(el) {
	var id = ATTRD(el);
	exports.tapi('redirects_read ERROR', { id: id }, function(response) {
		SET('formredirect @reset', response);
		SET('*form', 'formredirect');
	});
};
```

`formredirect`, the form's `CLASS`, the importer condition, `common.form` and `*form` must agree with the target shell. Do not copy the open function into another app without its alias/importer setup. Read data before showing an edit form; initialize a new model before showing create so the previous record does not leak into it.

## Form → submit → caller refresh

```html
<ui-component name="miniform" path="common.form" config="if:CLASS;title:@(Redirect);reload:?/reload;submit:?/submit;width:400" class="hidden" plugin="CLASS">
	<div class="padding">
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.url" config="required:1">@(URL)</ui-component>
		<ui-component name="input" path="?.target" config="required:1">@(Target URL)</ui-component>
	</div>
	<nav>
		<ui-component name="validate" path="?">
			<button name="submit" disabled>@(SUBMIT)</button>
			<button name="cancel">@(Cancel)</button>
		</ui-component>
	</nav>
</ui-component>

<script>
	PLUGIN(function(exports) {

		var caller;

		exports.reload = function() {
			caller = exports.caller;
		};

		exports.submit = function(hide) {
			var model = exports.form;
			exports.tapi('redirects_save ERROR', model, function() {
				hide();
				caller.exec('refresh');
			});
		};

	});
</script>
```

The form component owns the submit/cancel buttons. Ordinary screen buttons use `exec`; do not add a second submit listener. Hide only after a successful response, then refresh the caller. Verify `exports.form` / `exports.model` against the actual UI version and nearby form; they are not names to exchange mechanically.

## Binding and templates

Screens bind `?.items` through `ui-bind` and render a `script type="text/html"` with Tangular. Update the model (`exports.set('items', response)`) so the binding owns rendering, rather than keeping a parallel list in the DOM. Use `CLASS` for screen CSS, `?` for local paths and `data-exec="?/method"` for handlers. Preserve the shell's global model paths.

Treat user text as text in templates; do not add raw HTML rendering or string-built event attributes. Backend view directives (`@{...}`), translation markers (`@(...)`) and client Tangular (`{{ ... }}`) are distinct stages. Use the syntax supported by that app's library and compiler; check a working template for block terminators and escaping.

## Translations and icons

English text is the source key: `@(Save)`, `@(Target URL)`, translated through the app's `.resource` files. Keep resource keys, locale component configuration and any new error text synchronized. Avoid hard-coded translated copies in JS conditionals. Use the existing Total Icons `ti ti-*` assets and names from the app, with a label or accessible name for icon-only controls.

## Reusable components

Look for an existing component first. If new behaviour is reusable, use `COMPONENT('name', function(self, config, cls) { ... })` and the lifecycle supported by the installed jComponent version: build the DOM once, update from its bound value, react to configuration changes and release subscriptions/timers when destroyed. Read an existing component of that version for the exact methods. Keep feature permissions, API URLs and page model names in the plugin rather than baking them into the component.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/cms-widgets.md

# CMS widgets

A CMS widget is a reusable editable content block. Preserve the catalogue's native single-file format, `widgets/<id>.html`; a widget is not a jComponent registration or a standalone web page. Inspect the consuming CMS before choosing APIs: the reference CMS uses Framework 5 on the server and jComponent v19 in the admin. The backend major does not determine the browser UI major.

## Sections

| Section | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `<script total>` | Metadata and optional server hooks |
| `<settings>` | Editor controls and optional settings script/style |
| `<style>` | Widget CSS |
| `<body>` | Initial editable content |
| `<script>` outside settings/body | Optional public browser code |
| `<template>` | Optional render template |
| `<readme>` | Purpose, defaults, allowed values and dependencies |

Use exact lowercase section tags. The CMS extracts settings before other sections, so its nested script/style stay inside settings. Metadata follows existing widgets: `exports.id`, `name`, `author`, `version`, `preview`, and `config` when needed. Match the id and filename; check existing ids and names. Preview is an embedded image, not a separate required catalogue file.

## Scope and settings

The compiler replaces `CLASS` with `w-<normalized-widget-id>` in CSS, settings, body, public JS and template. That prefix belongs to the widget type and is shared by its instances. Scope CSS with `.CLASS`/`.CLASS-...`; change an individual instance through the `el` argument rather than a global selector or fixed DOM id.

Settings controls use `?.key` paths corresponding to defaults in `exports.config`. Their `<script>` may export `check(config, el)`, `load(config, el)` and `save(config, el)`. Defaults must match the initial body. Document finite values such as status/alignment explicitly; validate them before constructing classes or styles. Apply cosmetic changes without replacing edited text, repeated blocks or nested widgets. Repeated saves must be safe.

Use the existing editor markers where appropriate: `CMS_edit`, `CMS_remove`, `CMS_repeat`, `CMS_attribute` and `CMS_widgets` for nested content. Visitor content remains editable content, rather than being converted into fixed admin translation keys. Follow the consuming CMS's localization path for settings UI.

## Server rendering

A static widget normally needs no render hook. A dynamic widget may export `render(opt, next)` in `<script total>`. The CMS supplies instance configuration in `opt.config`, inner markup in `opt.html`, the whole body in `opt.body` and the render template in `opt.template`. Other page/user context is optional.

Call `next(content, replace, cache)` exactly once on success, empty and failure paths. The default keeps the wrapper; `replace: true` removes it. Cache only output that is safe to share within the CMS cache scope. Do not assume incoming saved config contains newly added defaults.

The server script is evaluated before scoping and is not rewritten: never return unresolved CLASS placeholders from a server render hook. Reuse scoped markup or emit known classes explicitly. Encode text inserted into server HTML with `.encode()`; use `.text()` in editor DOM. Public scripts cannot assume the admin's library or state is loaded on every site layout.

## Verification and AI guidance

Give agents the native format, actual hook contracts, compatible examples, a short creation/review workflow and commands that check the artifact. Keep a shared skill/checklist instead of divergent copies for each agent. Generate model indexes from the maintained pages and check links and commands. Preserve existing catalogue files when adding an authoring kit; tooling and examples do not need a catalogue migration.

Check with the real parser/compiler, then browser settings and published rendering. Test edited content, nested slots, repeated saves, two configurations, empty/long/HTML-like text and desktop/mobile widths. Open a screenshot of the final widget before accepting its appearance. Chromium can be installed by Playwright; Chrome is an alternative. An isolated browser harness does not prove complete CMS editor integration. See [native tests](../general/testing.md).

## References

- [CMS definitions/func.js](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/definitions/func.js): FUNC.recompile, sections and CLASS substitution.
- [CMS widget template](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/public/widget.txt), [editor](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/public/cmseditor/index.html), [admin layout](https://github.com/totaljs/cms/blob/2d3e9471c166a31e33ea9e93e32bb9a501ebcc9c/views/admin.html): hooks, markers and UI version.
- [Framework 5 cms.js](https://github.com/totaljs/framework5/blob/7d2d553fc774090081b4e3b1ae75a52ef06b42b8/cms.js): rendering, wrappers and cache.
- [CMS widget authoring kit](https://github.com/totaljs-es/cms-widgets/blob/63892ff/AGENTS.md): runnable examples, checks, skills and embedded previews.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/conventions/frontend/css.md

# CSS

- File names lowercase, words separated by `-`.
- **One rule per line**: keep all declarations of a selector on the same line.
- Strings in `'` apostrophes.
- No vendor prefixes. Put `/*auto*/` at the top of the file and Total.js adds them.
- No LESS and no SASS: Total.js CSS supports variables and nested selectors.

```css
/*auto*/

.class { key1: value; key2: value; key3: value; }
.class > div { key1: value; key2: value; }
```

## In plugins

Style that belongs to a screen goes at the top of its HTML file, scoped with `CLASS`:

```html
<style>
	.CLASS .listing2 figure { margin-bottom: 10px; }
	.CLASS .listing2 .permanent { background-color: #F6E7EA; }
</style>
```

`CLASS` becomes a class unique to the plugin, so the rule cannot leak to other screens.

## Predefined classes

The `intranetcss` component provides the common design (panels, toolbars, badges, messages, listings, tabs, dark mode). Use its classes before writing new CSS: see [components](components.md).

## Global style

`public/default.css` holds what is shared. Colors that change per user or theme are CSS variables (`:root { --color: ... }`), set once in the layout.

## Static files

`/img/`, `/css/`, `/js/`, `/fonts/`, `/videos/`. Images use the file-name rule: lowercase with dashes.

## Component skins

Scope overrides to an app class combined with the official component class, for example `.app-backtotop.ui-backtotop`. Keep the official component's selectors and behavior intact. Component CSS can be injected after the app stylesheet; use deliberate specificity instead of depending only on load order or broad global overrides.

Skinning the official BackToTop works this way. Preserve visible keyboard focus, sufficient contrast, mobile positioning and `prefers-reduced-motion` when adapting its appearance. Semantic or focus changes belong in a small native initialization hook, as described in [components](components.md), rather than in CSS.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/reference/total5-0.0.20.md

# Total.js 5: what 0.0.20 adds

The stable version of `total5` on npm is `0.0.19` (`latest`). Version `0.0.20` is the beta (`npm install total5@beta`, `0.0.20-3` when this page was written). An application with `"total5": "latest"` does not have what is on this page until 0.0.20 is the stable version: use a feature of this page only in a project that depends on `total5@beta` or on `0.0.20` and later, and say so.

Every example here was run with `0.0.20-3`. The source of the list is the `changelog.txt` of the framework.

## Actions as MCP tools

`$mcp : true` in the file `config` opens the route `POST /$mcp/`. Every action with `mcp: true` is a tool there. The comment of a field is the description of the argument, and the `summary` of the action is the description of the tool.

```js
NEWACTION('Items|create', {
	name: 'Create an item',
	summary: 'Creates an item and returns it',
	mcp: true,
	input: '*name:String // The name of the item',
	action: function($, model) {
		$.callback({ name: model.name });
	}
});
```

- The tool is named `Items_create`: a name of a tool cannot have the pipe.
- A client lists the tools with `tools/list` and calls one with `tools/call` and the arguments `{ input: {}, query: {}, params: {} }`.
- By default every caller is accepted as an administrator. An application that other programs reach replaces `Total.mcp.auth = function($) { ... }` with its own check, as it does with `AUTH`.

## The cache of an action

`cache` keeps the answer of an action for the same request, so the action does not run again.

```js
NEWACTION('Items|list', {
	name: 'List of items',
	query: 'search:String',
	cache: { query: true, expire: '1 minute' },
	action: function($) {
		$.callback(items);
	}
});
```

`query: true`, `params: true` and `input: true` make one entry for each different value of them; `user: true` makes one for each user and `language: true` one for each language. `expire` is how long it is kept (`'5 minutes'` by default). Two calls with `?search=a` ran the action once; a call with `?search=b` ran it again.

## Two types for the fields: `JSON` and `IP`

```js
input: '*name:String, meta:JSON, address:IP'
```

- `JSON` accepts a text that is valid JSON. The value stays a text: the action parses it with `model.meta.parseJSON()`.
- `IP` accepts an IP address.
- A wrong value answers 400 with the name of the field, as the other types do.

## An answer with its own content type

```js
ROUTE('GET /export/', function($) {
	$.content('id;name\n1;Anna\n', 'text/csv');
});
```

`$.content(value, type)` answers with that text and that `content-type`. Without a type it is `application/octet-stream`.

## The environment of an action

A caller can name the environment of a call, and the action reads it in `$.env`:

```js
var response = await ACTION('Mail|send', model).env('test').promise();
```

```js
action: function($, model) {
	if ($.env === 'test') {
		$.callback({ sent: false });
		return;
	}
	// ...
}
```

## Tests: a command and fakes

`total5 test` runs the tests of the folder `tests` of the project (or of the current folder): it loads `tests/config` when it exists, then `tests/init.js`, then every other `.js` file. `total5 test name1 name2` runs only those files. A test file only needs `Test.push()`: the command loads the framework and runs them.

```js
// tests/orders.js
Test.push('orders', async function(next) {

	// The action that sends the email is replaced: the test does not send anything
	Test.fake('Mail|send', {
		name: 'Fake',
		action: function($) {
			$.callback({ sent: 'fake' });
		}
	});

	var response = await ACTION('Orders|close').promise();
	Test.print('closing an order sends the email', response.sent === 'fake' ? null : 'failed');

	Test.restore();
	next();
});
```

`Test.fake(name, definition)` takes the definition of an action, as `NEWACTION` does, and `Test.restore()` puts the real actions back.

## Smaller additions

| Addition | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Total.FsPromises` | The module `node:fs/promises`, as `Total.Fs` is `node:fs` |
| `User` | A global class: `new User({ id: '1', name: 'Anna' })` copies the fields to the object |
| `U.validhost(host)` | `true` for a plain hostname or a canonical IP address: `example.com` and `127.0.0.1` are valid, `0x7f.0.0.1` is not |
| `U.tohost(host)` | The canonical form of a hostname (`EXAMPLE.com` is `example.com`, `bücher.de` is `xn--bcher-kva.de`), or an empty text when it is not valid |

## In the changelog and not tried here

- `QueryBuilder.autoqueryjson($, column, schema, [defsort], [maxlimit])`: `autoquery()` for the properties of a JSON column.
- `JSONSchema.toAIObject(name, [description])` and `JSONSchema.toAITool(name)`.
- `$.throw(err)` and `$.touch([url])` in actions and controllers.
- The fixes of `CRON()` with a step (`*/15`), of the mail attachments, of `AJAX()` with XML and the hardening of hostnames.

## A problem found in 0.0.20-3

`$.invalidsafe(msg, err)` in an action throws `ReferenceError: path is not defined` and the request ends in a timeout. Use `$.invalid(msg)` and log the error apart until a later version fixes it.

---

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/apps/contacts/readme.md

# Contacts

An API of contacts with Total.js 5: list, read, create, update and remove. The data goes through `DATA` (QueryBuilder) on the embedded NoSQL database (`DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')`), so the application needs nothing else to run. It can move to PostgreSQL later by taking the prefix `nosql/` away: see [`apps/contacts-postgresql`](../contacts-postgresql).

**The request it answers:** "Create an API for contacts (name, email and phone) with a token, without a database server."

**The shape:** an application without plugins. It fits a small service with one or two collections. An application that will grow by features is made with plugins.

| File | What it has |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Starts the framework |
| `config` | The name of the application and the token of the API |
| `package.json` | `total5` is the only dependency |
| `controllers/api.js` | The routes of the API, one line each |
| `schemas/contacts.js` | The actions: `Contacts|list`, `Contacts|read`, `Contacts|create`, `Contacts|update`, `Contacts|remove` |
| `definitions/auth.js` | Who the request is: the token of the header `x-token` |
| `test.js` | The tests: they start the application and call every action |

## Run it

```
npm install
node index.js 8000
```

Every request is a `POST` to `/api/` with the header `x-token` and the action in `schema`:

```
POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/
x-token: change-this-token
content-type: application/json

{ "schema": "contacts_create", "data": { "name": "Anna", "email": "anna@example.com" } }
```

| Schema | Data | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `contacts` or `contacts?search=an` | | the contacts, sorted by name |
| `contacts_read/{id}` | | the contact, or 404 |
| `contacts_create` | `name` (required), `email`, `phone` | `{ success: true, value: id }` |
| `contacts_update/{id}` | `name` (required), `email`, `phone` | `{ success: true, value: id }`, or 404 |
| `contacts_remove/{id}` | | `{ success: true, value: id }`, or 404 |

A request without the token is answered with 401, and a wrong field with 400 and the name of the field.

## Test it

```
node test.js
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/apps/contacts-postgresql/readme.md

# Contacts on PostgreSQL

The API of [`apps/contacts`](../contacts) with its data in PostgreSQL. Its routes and its authorization are the same files, and its actions are the same code: only the prefix `nosql/` of the table name is gone.

**The request it answers:** "My contacts API has grown: move its data to PostgreSQL."

**The shape:** an application without plugins, with `DATA` (QueryBuilder) on PostgreSQL. An application written with `DATA` from the start moves here by adding the definition of the database and taking the prefix `nosql/` away from its table names; no query is written again.

## What differs from apps/contacts

| File | In `apps/contacts` | Here |
|---|---|---|
| `schemas/contacts.js` | `DATA.find('nosql/tbl_contact')` | `DATA.find('tbl_contact')` |
| `definitions/db.js` | | `require('querybuilderpg').init('default', CONF.database, 1, ERROR('PostgreSQL'));` |
| `config` | | `database : postgresql://user:password@localhost/contacts` |
| `package.json` | | the dependency `querybuilderpg` |
| `database.sql` | | the table `tbl_contact` |
| `definitions/init.js` | | creates the table from `database.sql` the first time the application starts |

`controllers/api.js` and `definitions/auth.js` do not change, and `schemas/contacts.js` changes only in that prefix. A test checks both.

The table has the names of the SQL conventions, which the application used from the start: `tbl_contact`, `id` as `text` filled with `UID()`, `dtcreated` and `dtupdated`.

## Run it

Create the database and write its connection in `config`:

```
createdb contacts
npm install
node index.js 8000
```

The API is the one of `apps/contacts`.

## Test it

The tests need PostgreSQL and a database only for them, because they drop and create the table `tbl_contact` there:

```
createdb knowledge_test
node test.js
```

The connection is at the top of `test.js`. When PostgreSQL does not answer, the tests say `SKIPPED` and end with the code 3.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/apps/files/readme.md

# Files

An API to upload files and download them with Total.js 5. The files are kept in the file storage of the framework, so the application needs nothing else to run.

**The request it answers:** "Create an API where I can upload files and get an address to download each one."

**The shape:** an application without plugins. The files go to `FILESTORAGE`, which is made for them: it keeps each file with its name, size and type under an id. Records go through `DATA` (see `apps/contacts`); files do not go in a database.

| File | What it has |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Starts the framework |
| `config` | The name of the application and the token |
| `package.json` | `total5` is the only dependency |
| `controllers/api.js` | The routes: the API, the upload and the download |
| `schemas/files.js` | The actions: `Files|list`, `Files|upload`, `Files|remove` |
| `definitions/auth.js` | Who the request is: the token of the header `x-token` |
| `test.js` | The tests: they start the application, upload a real file, download it and remove it |

## The three kinds of route

```js
ROUTE('+API    ?           -files_remove/{id}     --> Files|remove');
ROUTE('+POST   /upload/    @upload <5MB           --> Files|upload');
ROUTE('FILE /download/*.*', download);
```

- The upload is a `POST` with `@upload` (a multipart form) and the biggest size it accepts, `<5MB`. A bigger request is answered with 431.
- The download is a `FILE` route: it has no `+`, so everybody who has the address of a file can read it. The id of a file cannot be guessed.

## Store, read and remove a file

```js
// The uploaded files are in $.files. Each one goes to the storage "files" with a new id
var meta = await $.files[i].fs('files', UID());
// meta: { id, name, size, ext, type, date }

// The list of the stored files
var items = await FILESTORAGE('files').browse().promise($);

// The file as the answer of a request, with its content type
FILESTORAGE('files').http($, { id: id, download: true });

// Remove it
FILESTORAGE('files').remove(id, function(err) { /* err when it does not exist */ });
```

The storage is the folder `databases/fs-files` of the application.

## Run it

```
npm install
node index.js 8000
```

```
curl -H "x-token: change-this-token" -F "file=@photo.jpg" http://127.0.0.1:8000/upload/
```

| Request | Answer |
|---|---|
| `POST /upload/` with one or more files | the stored files, each with its `url` |
| `POST /api/` with `{ "schema": "files" }` | the stored files |
| `POST /api/` with `{ "schema": "files_remove/{id}" }` | `{ success: true, value: id }`, or 404 |
| `GET /download/{id}.{ext}` | the file; with `?download=1` the browser saves it with its name |

The upload, the list and the removal need the header `x-token`. An upload without a file is answered with 400.

## Test it

```
node test.js
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/apps/website/readme.md

# Website

A small website with Total.js 5: a home page, a list of products and a page for each product. The pages are rendered on the server with views and one layout. There is no database: the content is a list in memory.

**The request it answers:** "Create a simple website for a bakery, with a home page and its products."

**The shape:** an application without plugins and without an API. It fits public pages that a person reads. An application with screens to manage data is made with plugins.

| File | What it has |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Starts the framework |
| `config` | The name of the website and the email of the footer |
| `package.json` | `total5` is the only dependency |
| `controllers/default.js` | The routes of the pages and the function of each one |
| `definitions/products.js` | The products, in `MAIN.products` |
| `views/layout.html` | The HTML that every page shares: head, header, footer |
| `views/index.html`, `products.html`, `product.html` | The content of each page |
| `public/css/default.css` | The styles |
| `test.js` | The tests: they start the application and read every page |

## How a page is made

A route calls its function, and the function renders a view with its data:

```js
ROUTE('GET /products/{id}/', product);

function product($) {
	var item = MAIN.products.findItem('id', $.params.id);
	if (!item) {
		$.fallback(404);
		return;
	}
	$.view('product', item);
}
```

The view reads the data as `model` and goes inside `views/layout.html`, where `@{body}` is:

```html
@{title(model.name)}

<h1>@{model.name}</h1>
<p class="price">@{model.price.format(2)} EUR</p>
```

- `@{title(...)}` sets the title of the page; the framework adds the name of the application to it.
- `@{import('meta', 'head', 'default.css')}` in the layout writes the title and loads `public/css/default.css`.
- `@(Text)` marks a text for translation.
- `CONF.name` and `CONF.email` are the settings of the file `config`.

## Run it

```
npm install
node index.js 8000
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

## Test it

```
node test.js
```

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/totaljs-es/knowledge/main/apps/board/readme.md

# Board

A board of tasks and notes with Total.js 5, made with plugins. Each feature is a plugin with its routes, its actions, its screen and its form, and the application shows them in a menu.

**The request it answers:** "Create an application to keep my tasks and my notes, where I can add more sections later."

**The shape:** an application with plugins. It fits an application with screens to manage data that will grow by features: a new feature is a new folder in `plugins/`, and nothing else changes. A small API or a website with a few pages does not need plugins.

| File | What it has |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Starts the framework |
| `config` | The name of the application; it listens only on this computer |
| `controllers/default.js` | The route of the page: it gives the layout the plugins that the user can see |
| `definitions/auth.js` | Who the request is: one local user |
| `definitions/init.js` | The components of the interface that the layout loads |
| `views/index.html` | The layout: the menu, a `page` for the screen of each plugin and an `importer` for its form |
| `public/css/default.css` | The styles of the layout |
| `plugins/tasks/`, `plugins/notes/` | The two features |
| `test.js` | The tests: they start the application and call the API of both plugins |

## A plugin

```
plugins/tasks/
	index.js              the name, the icon, the position in the menu and the routes
	schemas/tasks.js      the actions
	public/index.html     the screen
	public/form.html      the form that opens over the screen
```

The routes of a plugin are in its `index.js`, not in `controllers/`:

```js
exports.icon = 'ti ti-check-circle';
exports.name = '@(Tasks)';
exports.position = 1;

exports.install = function() {
	ROUTE('+API    ?    -tasks                   --> Tasks|list');
	ROUTE('+API    ?    +tasks_save              --> Tasks|save');
};
```

The files of `public/` are served under `/_tasks/`. The screen is a `<ui-plugin>` with one `PLUGIN(function(exports) { ... })`: `?.items` is the data of the plugin, `?/create` is `exports.create`, and `exports.tapi('tasks ERROR', callback)` calls the API and shows the error to the user.

The form is a `miniform` that the layout loads with an `importer`. The screen opens it with a model, and the form refreshes the screen after it saves:

```js
// the screen
exports.create = function() {
	SET('formtasks @default', {});
	SET('common.form', 'formtasks');
};

// the form
exports.submit = function(hide) {
	var model = exports.model;
	exports.tapi('tasks_save ERROR', { id: model.id, name: model.name, note: model.note }, function() {
		hide();
		PLUGINS.tasks.refresh();
	});
};
```

## Add a feature

Copy `plugins/notes` to a new folder, change its name, icon and position in `index.js`, and write its actions, screen and form. The layout finds it by itself.

## It has no sign in

One person uses it on their own computer: `$ip : 127.0.0.1` in the config and one user in `definitions/auth.js`. Before other people reach it, write a real check in `AUTH`, as the token of `apps/contacts`.

## Run it

```
npm install
node index.js 8000
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8000`. The first start downloads the components of the interface from `cdn.componentator.com`.

## Test it

```
node test.js
```

The tests call the API. The screens were checked in a browser: create, edit, mark as done and remove a task, and create a note.
